name: CD4052BM96
title: CMOS analog multiplexers/demultiplexers with logic-level conversion: CD4051B, CD4052B, CD4053B
summary: A family of three digitally addressed CMOS analog switches: the CD4051B single 8-channel multiplexer, the CD4052B differential 4-channel multiplexer and the CD4053B triple 2-channel switch. Separate VSS and VEE pins let 3 V to 20 V logic control analog signals up to 20 V peak to peak, including signals below logic ground. On resistance is a few hundred ohms at 5 V and falls to about 125 Ω at higher supply; off leakage is in the picoamp range.

circuits.title: Time-division link with the CD4052B
circuits.description: Four differential signal pairs share one two-wire link. On the sending side one CD4052B takes each pair on an X channel and the matching Y channel; its two commons feed a differential amplifier/line driver. On the receiving side a differential receiver feeds the commons of a second CD4052B, whose X and Y channels are the outputs.

circuits.title: 24-to-1 multiplexer addressing
circuits.description: Three CD4051B eight-channel multiplexers with their commons joined form a 24-input selector. Address lines A, B and C reach all three chips. Lines D and E drive the A and B inputs of half a CD4556, whose enable input is grounded; its outputs Q0, Q1 and Q2 go to the inhibit inputs of the first, second and third CD4051B.

operation.text: CD4051B: one 8-to-1 switch, set by address inputs A, B, C. CD4052B: a differential 4-to-1 pair, two sections X and Y sharing address inputs A and B. CD4053B: three independent 2-to-1 (single-pole double-throw) switches, each with its own control input A, B or C. All three have an inhibit input; a high level on it opens every channel.
Channels pass signals both ways. Used as a demultiplexer, the common OUT/IN pins take the input and the channel IN/OUT pins are the outputs.

The logic runs between VDD and VSS (3 V to 20 V); the switches run between VDD and VEE (signals up to 20 V peak to peak). With VDD - VSS = 3 V, VDD - VEE may go to 13 V; above 13 V, VDD - VSS must be at least 4.5 V. Example: VDD = +4.5 V, VSS = 0 V, VEE = -13.5 V switches signals from -13.5 V to +4.5 V under 0 V to 5 V control. Quiescent power stays very low across the whole supply range whatever the control inputs are doing.

Typical supply arrangements: VDD = 15 V with VEE = VSS = 0 V; VDD = 7.5 V, VSS = 0 V, VEE = -7.5 V; VDD = 5 V, VSS = 0 V, VEE = -10 V; VDD = 5 V, VSS = 0 V, VEE = -5 V. Address and inhibit logic 0 is VSS and logic 1 is VDD; the analog signal may swing anywhere from VEE to VDD.
Address decoding is on chip. Switching is break-before-make, so two channels are never on together during a change of address.

rON 125 Ω typical over a 15 V p-p signal range at VDD - VEE = 18 V; channel-to-channel rON matching 5 Ω typical at VDD - VEE = 15 V; off-channel leakage ±100 pA typical at VDD - VEE = 18 V; quiescent dissipation 0.2 µW typical at VDD - VSS = VDD - VEE = 10 V; input current 1 µA maximum at 18 V across the full package temperature range and 100 nA at 18 V and 25 °C. Ratings are given at 5 V, 10 V and 15 V, and every part is tested for quiescent current at 20 V.
Every address and inhibit input has the standard CMOS protection network. The parts are sensitive to electrostatic discharge.
Analog and digital multiplexing and demultiplexing, A/D and D/A conversion, signal gating.
Catalog: CD4051B, CD4052B, CD4053B. Automotive (Q100): CD4051B-Q1, CD4053B-Q1. Military (QML): CD4051B-MIL, CD4052B-MIL, CD4053B-MIL.
